name: Calculating the Winning Percentage of a Sports Team (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that receives from the user the number of games that a sports team won in a tournament of 12 games and calculates the winning percentage of that sports team. The program must ask for the number of the games won until the user enters a valid number.

comments.content: We need variable totalGames to store the total number of games in the tournament. This is required for calculating the percentage of the games that the sports team won. We initialize it to 12 because we have 12 games in the tournament.
We need to read and process the user input. To read the values that the user enters, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament.
We need to read the number that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the integer by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.

We need to validate the number that the user has entered and ask for a valid input as long as the user enters an invalid number. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the number that the user entered is an invalid number.

The input is an invalid number if it is outside the valid range, that is when the number that the user enters is negative or greater than the total number of games in the tournament.

The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters an integer that is negative (less than zero) or greater than the total number of games in the tournament. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to false, that is when the user enters a non-negative number that is less than or equal to the total number of games in the tournament.

Note that the logical or operator is true if one or the other or both operands are true.
We prompt the user to enter the number of games that the sports team won because the previous number was not a valid number.

The user has to enter another number because the previous number that the user entered was not a valid number. We read the next number that the user enters by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

We need to calculate the percentage of game that the sports team won by dividing the number of games won by the total number of games in the tournament. We store the result of the division into variable ratio.

Notice that both variables in the division are int and dividing an int by an int results in an int. Since we want to keep the fractional part, we need to cast one of the operands to a floating-point data type like double. When floating-point value won is divided by an integer value totalGames, the value of totalGames is promoted to a floating-point value automatically, before the division takes place; thus, producing a floating-point result.

We want to round the ratio to three decimal places. To do this, we need to instantiate a DecimalFormat object with a pattern. In this statement, the pattern defined by the string 0.### indicates that at least one digit should be printed to the left of the decimal point and should be a zero if the integer portion of the value is zero. It also indicates that the fractional portion of the value should be rounded to three digits.

This statement prints the calculated ratio to the default standard output stream. Note that the ratio is formatted to have maximum of three decimal places. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the formatted variable.
